title: Shared Ancestor
story: A family archive is kept as a search tree of member numbers: every number in a node's left branch is smaller than the node, every number in its right branch is larger. Two members, a and b, are both in the tree, and either one may be the smaller. Report the number of their nearest shared ancestor: the deepest node that has both of them at or below it, so a member counts as its own ancestor. The archive's reader has almost no memory: a list or a stack of the nodes along the way will not fit.

notes: 2 to 70 members, all numbers different, 1 to 1000.
a and b are two different members of the tree.
The tree can be as deep as it has members.

hints: Stand on a node and ask where a and b are. If both are smaller than it, their shared ancestor is in the LEFT branch; if both are larger, it is in the RIGHT branch.
Otherwise the two go different ways here, or one of them is this very node: this node is the answer. One variable that walks down from the root is enough.
WHILE the node IS NOT NOTHING: IF a AND b are both LESS THAN its NODE VALUE, SET the node to its LEFT; ELSE IF both are GREATER THAN it, SET the node to its RIGHT; ELSE RETURN the NODE VALUE.
edgeCases: one member is the ancestor of the other
both members deep in one branch
a tree as deep as it is large: the way down does not fit in memory
